name: Land surveyor

pf.license.need: Each surveyor who leads a survey and signs the plat holds their own state professional surveyor license. A crew member works under the licensed surveyor in charge, who signs. The company holds a firm license or registration where the state asks. Only a licensed surveyor signs a survey drawing.
pf.license.ask: Each surveyor's license number, type and state. The firm's license or registration number, where the state's form asks for one.
pf.license.who_holds: Each licensed surveyor holds their own license. The firm holds its own registration where required. A crew chief who is not licensed never signs.
pf.license.check: none: Rosie never looks up, checks or confirms a license, insurance or registration (D96); anything shown is as given by the business, not checked by Rosie
pf.license.blocks_live: Where the state licenses surveyors: no survey is offered until the firm's and the surveyor's numbers check out. A signed survey is offered only with a licensed surveyor in charge.
pf.license.insurance_bond: Professional liability (errors-and-omissions) insurance where the state's form requires it. Shown as given by the business, not checked by Rosie.
pf.license.background_checks: Only where the state's rules require them, or as the business's own word.
pf.license.shown_to_customers: The surveyor's license number on the survey agreement, offers, confirmations and the signed survey, where the state's rules require it.
pf.license.not_this_work: Legal advice on a boundary or title dispute, title insurance, building or fencing work, and a boundary opinion the records and the markers on the ground do not support. A survey shows where the lines are by the records and what the crew finds; it does not settle who owns the land.

pf.services.pattern: Set service: one fieldwork visit at the property, priced by the lot's size, with a signed survey drawing later.

list.name: Boundary survey
list.price_kind: set by the customer's answers (lot size, and whether the corners are marked)
list.example: lot up to ¼ acre: $495; ¼ to ½ acre: $595; ½ to 1 acre: $695 (the example business's own prices)
list.length: about 3 hours in the field for a crew of two; the signed survey and the corner markers follow in about 10 business days
list.where: at the property; nobody needs to be there
list.money: a deposit at booking, the rest on the bill after the signed survey is delivered

list.name: Corner re-stake
list.example: $150, about 1 hour: marks reset at the corners of a lot already surveyed
list.money: booked like the first survey; paid in full when booking (the example business's setting)

list.name: Construction staking (the second kind of work)
list.example: the corners and the building layout marked for a new build

list.name: Topographic survey
list.price_kind: set by the surveyor at the visit from the tract's size and terrain; only the $89 trip fee is promised before
list.example: a wooded tract: priced after a walk-through; the fee never depends on where the lines fall

list.name: Large lot or complex boundary
list.price_kind: quoted from the deed, old plats and aerial photos first
list.example: a 5-acre parcel: $640, with a deposit; Sam OKs any quote over $500

list.name: Elevation certificate
list.example: $199 (a flood-zone elevation reading); $249 when Sam goes himself

list.name: Fence line location
list.price_kind: one price, an add-on at the visit
list.example: $160: the existing fence shown on the drawing, only if the client says yes first

list.name: Trip fee
list.example: $89: only for a late cancel or no way in that Sam confirms, or a return trip when the ground was not safe or the locate was not done

list.name: Records consult, plat lookups and survey reviews (at Lee Survey Office)
list.example: 30-minute records consult $35; plat lookup $20; survey review, reading an old survey with you, $40; second look at another firm's survey $55; subdivision planning meeting, about 2½ hours, $140; at the property $75 (the example office's own prices)
list.where: at the office, by video, or at the property
list.money: card saved for the $20 fee; paid at the office after

pf.services.start_times: A 2-hour arrival window, like 8 to 10am. The crew's exact time is texted on the way.
pf.services.notice: 2 days' notice by default, plus the time the utility locate takes (about 2 business days). A sooner time only if Sam says yes.
pf.services.capacity: One crew per survey. Construction staking only with a crew that does it.
pf.services.nobody_home: Yes: nobody needs to be there. The crew works outdoors; a gate code, if any, is set at booking and shown only to the crew on the day. The owner is welcome to meet the crew.
pf.services.online: Records consults, plat lookups and survey reviews can be done by video.
pf.services.not_offered: Legal advice, title insurance, fencing or building work, and any promise of where a line falls.
pf.services.partner_work: None. Rosie never names or refers another business.

before_times: The town or ZIP, and what kind of land: a lot in a neighborhood, a rural parcel, or a large tract
About how big the lot is, and whether the corners are marked now
What the survey is for: a fence, an addition, buying or selling, a boundary question, or a permit
Do you own the land, or do you have the owner's yes?
after_a_time: Dogs or other animals on the land, and where they'll be
Is the land fenced, gated or overgrown?
secure_page_only: The street address or the parcel number
A gate or lock code, typed only by whoever sets it up
The deed, an earlier survey, a title commitment and any plans
pf.questions.who_may_book: An adult 18 or older who owns the land or acts for the owner (an agent, an attorney, a builder with the owner's written yes). A neighbor or a tenant never books a survey of land they do not own. The client named on the survey agreement signs it.

words: a threat from someone at the property
what_happens: A gas smell or hissing near a marked line, sparks or smoke: everyone leaves the area first, then calls 911 and the gas company from outside. No booking until it is safe.
Live wires hanging down: stay away from that area, and call 911 if anyone is in danger. The survey can be booked for the rest of the land; the crew will not enter that area.
A threat from someone at the property: the booking is paused and Sam is told at once. 911 is given for anyone in danger. The crew never works where it feels unsafe.
pf.safety.booking_goes_on: No, for a gas smell or hissing, sparks, smoke or a threat. Yes, with the unsafe area left out, for live wires. A boundary dispute with a neighbor is not a threat: the booking goes on.

pf.first_steps.agreement: The business's own survey agreement (the kind of survey, what is delivered, the right to enter the land, and the fee), signed on the secure page before the time is booked. Rosie never writes or edits it.
pf.first_steps.locate: A utility locate request for the corners, made by Sam before the crew drives any marker into the ground, where the state's rules require it. It takes about 2 business days, or what the state's rules set; the first open times start after it.
pf.first_steps.documents: The deed, an earlier survey, a title commitment and any plans, added on the secure page if there are any.
prep_for_reminder: Leave any corner markers, flags or stakes where they are
Dogs and other animals put away or kept in the house
Gates unlocked or the code on the secure page; a path cut through thick brush if you can
Cars and sheds moved off any line you know about

pf.visit.check_in: If the owner meets the crew, they give the check-in code at the start. If nobody is there, DONE with photos confirms the visit.
pf.visit.entry_codes: A gate or lock code is shown only to the crew, only on the day, and each view is logged.
pf.visit.what_is_checked: The records are compared with the markers and fences on the ground; corners are found or set with caps and flagged; photos of each corner are taken. Anything the crew can't reach or find is noted in the drawing.
pf.visit.not_found: A corner that can't be found or reached is listed as not found. A return trip is offered for the trip fee, with the client's OK.
pf.visit.walk_through: If the owner is there, the crew shows the flagged corners. Where a line falls is in the signed survey only; the crew gives no legal opinion on the spot.
pf.visit.changes_at_visit: An add-on (an elevation certificate, a fence line location) only if the client says yes first, priced before it is done. The fee never depends on where the lines fall.
pf.visit.proof_done: DONE from the crew chief's phone, with photos of the corners. The signed survey follows by the date promised.
pf.visit.report: A signed survey drawing sent on a secure link by the date promised at booking (the example: 10 business days). A later date is told to the client before the old one passes. Rosie tracks the date.
pf.visit.report_release: Sam picks per service: the signed survey goes out at once, or once the bill is paid. Where the state's rules forbid holding it, it goes out at once.

pf.money.start: Boundary surveys: a deposit when booking, the rest on the bill after the signed survey is delivered. Consults at the office: a card saved for the fee, paid at the office after.
pf.money.other_ways: Nothing taken and the bill texted after; paid in full when booking (a corner re-stake); a deposit and the rest on the bill for a large lot quoted first.
pf.money.deposits: A deposit of about half of a set-price survey; the cap, if any, comes from the state form. The rest is paid after the signed survey is delivered.
pf.money.fees: Late cancel, or no way in at the arrival window: the business's own trip fee (the example: $89). A return trip when the ground was not safe or the locate was not done: the trip fee. Sam confirms each one; no answer, no fee.
pf.money.fee_rule: The fee never depends on where the lines fall, on a neighbor's agreement, or on the sale closing.
pf.money.tax: A sales tax line only where the state taxes survey services, from the state form.

never_in_texts: The street address or parcel number in a first text to someone new
The signed survey or where any line falls: only the secure link
A boundary dispute's details: only the secure page
pf.messages.who_gets_texts: The client. A neighbor or anyone else only after their own yes.
pf.messages.minors: Nobody under 18 books or signs the survey agreement.

skills: Records consults and survey reviews at the office
pf.staff.licenses: Each licensed surveyor's own license, where the state licenses surveyors. Only a licensed surveyor signs a drawing.
pf.staff.stand_in: Another crew led by a licensed surveyor with the same skills may stand in, with the client's OK first.
pf.staff.supervision: A crew member or surveyor-in-training works under the licensed surveyor in charge, who signs the drawing.
pf.staff.who_oks: Sam OKs quotes over $500 and every fee. Pat, the office manager, may too; Sam's answer wins.

pf.rules.agreement: A signed survey agreement before the fieldwork starts, with the right to enter the land, where the state's rules require it.
pf.rules.locate: No marker is driven into the ground before the utility locate is done, where the state's rules require one. A visit waits for it, with no fee to the customer.
pf.rules.report_deadline: The signed survey reaches the client by the date promised at booking. A later date is told to the client before the old one passes. Rosie tracks the date.
pf.rules.fee_independence: The fee can't depend on where the lines fall, on a neighbor's agreement or on the sale closing.
pf.rules.no_legal_opinion: A survey shows where the lines are by the records and what the crew finds. It does not settle who owns the land: Rosie says a lawyer can help with that.
pf.rules.license_shown: The license number on offers, confirmations and the signed survey, where the state's rules require it.
pf.rules.records: 10 years, or longer where the state's rules ask: the agreement, the field notes, the photos and the drawing.

matter_most: The utility locate is late or marks a line at a corner: the visit waits or the marker moves, with no fee to the customer.
A corner is buried or can't be found: the crew uses the records to set it where they can, lists what was not found, and a return trip is offered for the trip fee.
Thick brush, snow or standing water makes the fieldwork unsafe or unreliable: the visit moves to the next good day, with no fee.
A neighbor won't allow the crew onto their land: the crew works the owner's land only, and the drawing says so.
The client asks the surveyor to put a line where the client wants it: declined; the survey shows where the records and the ground put it.
A boundary dispute with a neighbor: Rosie gives no legal advice; the booking goes on, and a lawyer can help with the dispute.
The client asks for fencing or building: Rosie says this business doesn't do it.
The signed survey runs late: the client hears the new date before the old one passes.
Nobody is there and a gate code doesn't work: the crew texts it, and the owner gets a link to send the right one.
pf.edges.rest: All other edge cases are handled the generic way.

notes:
Kept words: 'Trip fee' (the $89 fee for a late cancel or no way in, the parent's word too), 'Grace' (the master's grace time), 'leak' and 'color' (the master's shared safety and fairness lines, S13-40 lists color among protected traits).
New profession on the REDESIGN 2 master (batch S1, Tue Oct 27 2026), started from the refitted inspector overlay (set 'from'): a boundary survey is a set fieldwork visit at the property with a signed document later, and the agreement is signed before booking, like an inspection. It differs on purpose: the work is outdoors, nobody needs to be there, a crew arrives in a 2-hour window (flow B), and the money is a deposit with the rest on the bill after the signed survey. The parent's lockbox, agent-access and walk-through steps are not carried; the master's own check-in (the code at the door, or DONE with photos when nobody is there) stands.
Flow B is the usual side: Lee Land Surveying (boundary surveys of lots and large parcels, with construction staking as the second kind of work). Flow A is Lee Survey Office, Sam's office: a 30-minute records consult, plat lookups, survey reviews and a subdivision planning meeting, at the office, by video or at the property.
Prices are the example business's own: boundary survey $495 (lot up to a quarter acre), corner re-stake $150 (paid in full), elevation certificate $199 ($249 when Sam goes), fence line location $160, a large parcel quoted from the deed, old plats and aerial photos at $640 (Sam OKs over $500), a topographic survey priced at the visit by size, trip fee $89. Flow A: records consult $35, plat lookup $20, survey review $40, second look at a survey $55, subdivision planning meeting $140, at the property $75.
Money, flow B: main list|deposit|bill (a $250 deposit when booking, the $245 rest on the bill after the signed survey), list|none|bill (the bill after; the signed survey goes out once it is paid), list|full|none (a corner re-stake paid in full), photos|deposit|bill (a large parcel: $320 deposit, $320 on the bill). Flow A: list|card|counter (main), list|none|counter, list|full|none, list|card|card. The deposit cap, if any, comes from the state form. The fee never depends on where the lines fall.
Who must not be booked (pf.questions, pf.rules): anyone under 18; a neighbor or tenant for land they do not own; a request to put a line where the client wants it; legal advice on a boundary dispute (Rosie says a lawyer can help, and the booking goes on). A boundary dispute is not a threat; a threat from someone at the property pauses the booking.
Danger words (pf.safety): a gas smell or hissing, sparks or smoke, a threat from someone at the property (no booking until safe); live wires hanging down (booking goes on, that area left out). The danger-first call (B3-11, B3-18) uses a power line down in the yard, so the two steps read as one conversation. 'A fence line', 'a neighbor' and 'a boundary question' are the everyday reasons to book and are not stop words.
Settings: arrive a 2-hour window in flow B and a set start in flow A; cutoff 6pm the day before; booking choices B: a set time, windows. Nothing is sent now. The utility locate is a first step with a lead time (fact `firststeps`): own step B6-x01 gives Sam the to-do; the first open times start after it. The signed survey date in the examples is the next day (Fri Oct 23) like the parent's; the real turnaround is the owner's setting (the plug-in's example: 10 business days).
Rename pairs: only the inspector's pairs that match the frozen master were kept and re-worded for surveying; the arrival-window pairs ('8:30am' set starts) were dropped so flow B keeps the master's windows. Addresses and license numbers are made up (EX-1042 style). The master's 'Leak repair' sign-up row reads 'Topographic survey' (priced at the visit by size).
For the verifier: the deposit-first main path (about half up front) is the usual surveyor practice but is the example owner's choice; the plug-in leaves the share and cap to the owner and the state form. A boundary survey does not settle ownership: Rosie says so and points to a lawyer.
